tEn: How Clay Builds GTM Agents: Jeff Barg on AI, Spreadsheets, and the GTM Engineer
tZh: Clay 如何构建 GTM 智能体：Jeff Barg 谈 AI、表格与 GTM 工程师
sEn: Jeff Barg, Head of AI at Clay, explains how Clay turned the spreadsheet into a platform for GTM agents and coined the GTM engineer.
sZh: Clay 人工智能负责人 Jeff Barg 讲述 Clay 如何把表格变成 GTM 智能体平台，并塑造出“GTM 工程师”这一角色。

consensus.en: Go-to-market is a creative engineering discipline; Clay is built for the GTM engineer persona.
consensus.zh: Go-to-market 是一门创造性的工程学科；Clay 是为 GTM 工程师这一核心人群打造的。

consensus.en: Clay agents should do what sales reps did: qualify, enrich, and research across the whole table.
consensus.zh: Clay 智能体应完成销售代表的工作：在整张表上做资格筛选、数据丰富与研究。

consensus.en: Model routing matters: frontier intelligence for orchestration, cheaper models for simple tasks.
consensus.zh: 模型路由很重要：编排层用前沿智能，简单任务用更便宜的模型。

consensus.en: Most users hate the model selector; auto mode should beat manual selection at task level.
consensus.zh: 大多数用户讨厌模型选择器；自动模式应在任务层面胜过手动选择。

consensus.en: Post-training and open-weight models are becoming viable mainly for cost and speed gains.
consensus.zh: 后训练与开放权重模型正变得可行，主要为了降本提速。

consensus.en: Institutional courage is the most important thing at companies right now; keep pushing.
consensus.zh: 机构勇气是当下公司最重要的东西；要持续坚持推动。

contrarian.en: Don't make your own agent markedly better than Clay plus Claude Code; expose the platform to all agents.
contrarian.zh: 不要让自己的智能体明显强于 Clay 加 Claude Code；应把平台开放给所有智能体。

contrarian.en: Training a frontier model is still really hard; most companies jump into post-training too early.
contrarian.zh: 训练前沿模型仍然极难；大多数公司过早投入后训练。

contrarian.en: Cost savings only matter above roughly $10-100M inference spend; below that it's premature.
contrarian.zh: 只有推理支出达到约 1000 万至 1 亿美元以上，降本才有意义；低于此则过早。

contrarian.en: Agents are still bad at diagnosing their own traces; self-improvement loops mostly don't work.
contrarian.zh: 智能体仍不擅长诊断自己的轨迹；自我改进闭环大多行不通。

contrarian.en: MCP is not the endgame; the team shifted focus to a CLI, and form factor shouldn't matter much.
contrarian.zh: MCP 并非终局；团队已转向 CLI，接口形态本不该那么重要。

contrarian.en: Modern data stack is cooked; Clay hand-rolls most product data infrastructure on Postgres and ClickHouse.
contrarian.zh: 现代数据栈已经过时；Clay 大部分产品数据基础设施在 Postgres 和 ClickHouse 上手写。

turns.en: We have Jeff Lar here from Clay. You are the head of AI. Could you maybe introduce yourself and the business?
turns.zh: 我们请到了 Clay 的 Jeff Lar。你是 AI 负责人。能介绍一下你自己和公司吗？

turns.en: Yeah, absolutely. Well, first, thanks for having me. So, yeah, I'm Jeff. I've been at Clay for about 2 years. And Clay, we like to think of ourselves as a creative tool for growth. And so, really what that means is we help people build lists of companies and contacts for the purpose of prospecting or getting customers or finding new and great customers for their business. So, we help qualify those lists using agents and other data providers to basically add data points like the amount of revenue or funding they've gotten or who their CEO is or different locations that they have and use that to basically filter down to figure out who their best customers are.
turns.zh: 当然可以。首先，感谢邀请。我是 Jeff，在 Clay 工作了大约两年。Clay，我们喜欢把自己看作一个增长创意工具。这意味着我们帮助人们建立公司和联系人列表，用于拓客或获取客户，或者为他们的业务找到新的优质客户。我们使用智能体和其他数据提供商来筛选这些列表，基本上就是添加数据点，比如营收或融资额、CEO 是谁、不同地点等，然后用这些数据来筛选，找出谁是他们最好的客户。

turns.en: For those watching on YouTube, you are actually really identified with this spreadsheet for some reason. When I talk about the spreadsheet form factor with other AI builders, they usually point to Clay as the success example.
turns.zh: 对于在 YouTube 上观看的观众来说，你实际上因为某种原因与这个电子表格紧密相关。当我与其他 AI 构建者谈论电子表格形式时，他们通常指向 Clay 作为成功案例。

turns.en: Yes. And yeah, it's funny. I mean, Clay started seven years ago really as a low code tool in the spreadsheet. So, it makes a lot of sense. We've been around for a while and really have built up on that spreadsheet.
turns.zh: 是的。而且，这很有趣。Clay 七年前起步时，确实是一个电子表格中的低代码工具。所以这很合理。我们已经存在一段时间了，并且确实是在电子表格上发展起来的。

turns.en: And then I'll also identify you said it's a creative something. There's nothing creative here. It says build systems to grow revenue. That sounds a lot more like let's make money.
turns.zh: 然后我还要指出，你说它是创意什么的。这里没什么创意。上面写着“构建系统以增长营收”。这听起来更像是“让我们赚钱”。

turns.en: So creative.
turns.zh: 所以是创意。

turns.en: Yeah. Actually, give us two seconds on why are you guys always so cheery and not noticeable? Like Clay's branding is really on point.
turns.zh: 是的。实际上，给我们两秒钟说说为什么你们总是那么愉快而不显眼？Clay 的品牌形象真的很到位。

turns.en: Well, I do think it's a core part of the thesis that go to market really is a creative endeavor. And I don't know, I think actually none of our competitors really seem to believe that or try to do that. And I think it just adds to the ethos. I think it helps us build this community of people who try really cool and creative stuff to grow their companies.
turns.zh: 嗯，我确实认为这是核心论点的一部分：市场推广确实是一种创意活动。我不知道，我认为实际上我们的竞争对手似乎都不相信这一点，或者尝试这样做。我认为这增加了我们的精神气质。我认为它帮助我们建立了一个社区，人们尝试非常酷和创意的东西来发展他们的公司。

turns.en: Did you guys start that way by the way? Like the business was always this?
turns.zh: 顺便问一下，你们一开始就是这样吗？业务一直是这样吗？

turns.en: I think we've always spent a lot of time thinking about brand and how we present. But no, we really narrowed in on go to market. This was before I joined the company, but I think around 3 years ago, we really focused in on we were deciding like, oh, should we focus on recruiting or should we focus on go to market? Focus on go to market and then really double down there.
turns.zh: 我认为我们一直花很多时间思考品牌和如何呈现。但不，我们确实聚焦于市场推广。这在我加入公司之前，但我想大约三年前，我们真正专注于决定：哦，我们应该专注于招聘还是市场推广？专注于市场推广，然后真正加倍投入。

turns.en: Yeah. What was the reason for that? Just like a thesis.
turns.zh: 是的。原因是什么？就像一个论点。

turns.en: Um, there's this like little nice history chart. I don't know what this plays, but
turns.zh: 嗯，有一个不错的历史图表。我不知道这播放什么，但

turns.en: Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. I mean, I don't know. I mean,
turns.zh: 是的。是的。是的。我是说，我不知道。我是说，

turns.en: there was probably a lot of evolution in the 5 years that this started, but we really started with a bunch of different kind of ways to think about the company or think about the business, but it started very horizontal and then I think we just really wanted to focus in on kind of a singular persona. And that helped us sort of build the things that ended up really making Clay successful.
turns.zh: 在开始的五年里可能有很多演变，但我们确实从多种不同的思考公司或业务的方式开始，但一开始非常横向，然后我认为我们真的想聚焦于单一用户画像。这帮助我们构建了最终让 Clay 成功的东西。

turns.en: Cool. I think you know the thing that a lot of people tell me about Clay is that there's a lot of parallels with how I grew Lat Space and AIE because I identified this sort of segment of the market called that I call the AI engineer and I really focus on serving them and you guys are basically synonymous with the GTM engineer now. Can you describe what that is? You know I think this is one of the reasons why it's interesting for Basil and I to be on this pod because Basil is focusing on the FTE you guys are on the GTME and I'm on the AIE. You know we really branded this term the good market engineer and the idea was just companies in let's say the 2010s really spent a lot of time trying to build pipeline or trying to grow their companies through just throwing more people at the problem. You can probably just engineer a lot of these problems like you can probably actually build systems to find customers for you and I think this kind of coincided with LLM and the post ChatGPT era where you could actually have agents go and crawl the web or qualify customers and basically exert judgment at scale that way. And so, you know, you kind of had this confluence of things where you had these new systems that could effectively qualify or score accounts for you and just kind of a continued trend towards automation in the space and we were seeing more people basically engineering go to market systems and tried to brand that term around it.
turns.zh: 酷。我想你知道很多人告诉我关于 Clay 的事情是，这和我如何发展 Lat Space 和 AIE 有很多相似之处，因为我确定了这个市场细分，我称之为 AI 工程师，我真的专注于服务他们，而你们现在基本上就是 GTM 工程师的代名词。你能描述一下那是什么吗？你知道我认为这是 Basil 和我上这个播客有趣的原因之一，因为 Basil 关注 FTE，你们关注 GTME，而我关注 AIE。你知道我们真的把这个术语品牌化为“市场推广工程师”，想法就是公司在 2010 年代真的花了很多时间试图建立管道或试图通过向问题投入更多人来发展公司。你很可能可以直接工程化很多这些问题，比如你实际上可以构建系统来为你找到客户，我认为这与 LLM 和 ChatGPT 后时代相吻合，你可以让智能体去爬网或筛选客户，基本上以这种方式大规模施加判断。所以，你有了这些新系统的汇合，可以有效地为你筛选或评分账户，以及该领域自动化的持续趋势，我们看到越来越多的人基本上在工程化市场推广系统，并试图围绕它品牌化这个术语。

turns.en: What was the role of a person doing that before? I'm sure people have tried to do this for a long time, but I think it's sort of, you know, if you were to think about the different disciplines that go into good to market engineering, it's probably some agent engineering to figure out how to write the best prompts to actually qualify something, right? So, it's actually, you know, understanding LLM systems. There's probably some data engineering in there, right? Like you're actually building a bunch of lists, you're transforming them, you're enriching them, you're filtering down and building different views on top of that.
turns.zh: 之前做这个的人的角色是什么？我确信人们尝试这样做已经很久了，但我认为这有点像是，你知道，如果你考虑进入市场推广工程的不同学科，可能有一些智能体工程，弄清楚如何编写最佳提示来实际筛选某些东西，对吧？所以，这实际上是，你知道，理解 LLM 系统。可能还有一些数据工程，对吧？就像你实际上在构建一堆列表，你转换它们，你丰富它们，你筛选并在此基础上构建不同的视图。

turns.en: And there's sort of just regular software engineering built in there, too, right? You're orchestrating systems that when someone fills out a get-in-touch form on your website, probably research that company and then maybe send it to a rep or send it to an outbound campaign, right? All these sort of things that are kind of just traditional software engineering.
turns.zh: 而且这里面也包含了一些常规的软件工程，对吧？你在编排系统，当有人在你的网站上填写联系表单时，可能会研究那家公司，然后也许把它发送给销售代表或发送到外呼活动，对吧？所有这些事情都算是传统的软件工程。

turns.en: Yeah, I think the old school name for this might be marketing engineer, ops person. I may have even heard of it. Software engineer might be part of it, but a growth engineer might as well be a part of it.
turns.zh: 是的，我觉得这个岗位的老派叫法可能是营销工程师、运营人员。我可能还听说过。软件工程师可能是其中一部分，但增长工程师也可能是其中一部分。

turns.en: But growth maybe is more focused on marketing and yours is more sales, right?
turns.zh: 但增长可能更侧重于营销，而你的更侧重于销售，对吧？

turns.en: Yeah, I think probably this function would have fallen into revenue operations. That's probably the bucket of things, and still today we sell into revenue operations teams. But yeah, I think it's somewhat distinct as a discipline. I'd say it's pretty new.
turns.zh: 是的，我觉得这个职能可能原本会归入收入运营。那大概是它的范畴，而且今天我们仍然向收入运营团队销售。但没错，我认为它作为一个学科有些独特。我得说它相当新。

turns.en: What kinds of backgrounds do successful go-to-market engineers have?
turns.zh: 成功的市场推广工程师通常有什么样的背景？

turns.en: Oh man, it's pretty across the board. I think we've seen a lot of traditional software engineers move into the role, and so that's been pretty interesting to see—people approaching the problem from very first-principles software engineering standpoints. Definitely ambitious RevOps folks have grown into the role as well. So we've seen all different directions of people move into it.
turns.zh: 哦，天哪，相当多样化。我觉得我们看到很多传统软件工程师转入这个岗位，所以看到人们从非常第一性原理的软件工程角度来解决问题，这很有趣。肯定也有雄心勃勃的收入运营人员成长到这个岗位。所以我们看到人们从各个方向进入这个领域。

turns.en: Yeah. I think one of the things that people who have never done this job before don't really appreciate is that basically there is a lot of data mining and entity resolution and a little bit of knowledge graphs, maybe you can talk about that—just to get all these lists for people just for prospecting.
turns.zh: 是的。我觉得从未做过这份工作的人不太了解的一点是，基本上这里面有大量的数据挖掘和实体解析，还有一点知识图谱，也许你可以谈谈这个——只是为了给人们获取所有这些列表用于 prospecting。

turns.en: Yeah. I'm not sure—I think there's probably other use cases other than prospecting. Obviously a list is a very powerful thing that combines a lot of information. Multiple tens of billions of dollar companies are created just as a database that feeds into Clay. So my canonical examples are ZoomInfo or RocketReach—you've heard of all these things—where you need enrichment from just an email. That's all I have: okay, what company do they work at, what size is that company, are they the buyer, did they just move companies? I don't know what other details are relevant there. Definitely Clay—we sit in the market. We work with a bunch of different data providers and partners. So many—
turns.zh: 是的。我不确定——我觉得除了 prospecting 可能还有其他用例。显然，列表是一个非常强大的东西，它结合了大量信息。多家数百亿美元的公司就是作为数据库创建的，为 Clay 提供数据。所以我的典型例子是 ZoomInfo 或 RocketReach——你听说过所有这些——你需要从仅仅一个电子邮件进行丰富。这就是我所有的：好吧，他们在哪家公司工作，那家公司有多大，他们是买家吗，他们刚换了公司吗？我不知道还有哪些其他细节是相关的。当然，Clay——我们位于市场之中。我们与许多不同的数据提供商和合作伙伴合作。很多——

turns.en: A number, but you know, in the hundreds?
turns.zh: 一个数字，但你知道，是数百吗？

turns.en: In the hundreds for sure. And it's really flexible as a platform. If I think about other competitors or different people who have tried to build sales tools in the past, I think a lot of people try to build point solutions, and Clay is really generic, right? To your point, you can build a lot of stuff with lists, and we've seen people build crazy things in Clay, and that's intentional. And that comes with a bunch of trade-offs. Being very flexible means there are a lot of ways you can make mistakes. There are a lot of different ways you can build systems that don't work as you'd expect, but it becomes really powerful.
turns.zh: 肯定是数百。而且它作为一个平台非常灵活。如果我想到其他竞争对手或过去尝试构建销售工具的不同人，我觉得很多人试图构建点解决方案，而 Clay 非常通用，对吧？正如你所说，你可以用列表构建很多东西，我们看到人们在 Clay 中构建疯狂的东西，这是有意为之的。这伴随着一系列权衡。非常灵活意味着有很多方式可能犯错。有很多不同的方式可以构建出不如你预期的系统，但它变得非常强大。

turns.en: Can we take a step back to when you started Avenue and then maybe how that led you to joining Clay? So, yeah. Could you describe Avenue a little bit?
turns.zh: 我们能回溯一下你创办 Avenue 的时候，然后也许谈谈那如何引导你加入 Clay 吗？所以，是的。你能稍微描述一下 Avenue 吗？

turns.en: So, I joined Clay through the acquisition of my previous company, Avenue, which was a company I co-founded with a friend of mine from high school.
turns.zh: 所以，我通过我的前公司 Avenue 的收购加入了 Clay，那是我和一位高中朋友共同创办的公司。

turns.en: It's up on screen.
turns.zh: 它在屏幕上。

turns.en: Yeah, the website's still up. So Avenue was a company we started in early 2020. I built this with a friend of mine from high school. We had actually been building apps together back in middle school and high school. So we had one of the first 500 iPad apps on the iPad store back in the day.
turns.zh: 是的，网站还在。Avenue 是我们 2020 年初创办的公司。我和一位高中朋友一起构建了它。我们从初中和高中就一起开发应用。所以当年我们在 iPad 商店上有首批 500 个 iPad 应用之一。

turns.en: Nice.
turns.zh: 不错。

turns.en: So we'd always been tinkering on ideas, and my co-founder had worked at Uber, I worked at Amazon out of school, and we both wanted to start something together. Both had the idea of hey, we're working on different types of ops problems in very different domains, but it makes sense that these marketplace operations teams actually need observability solutions like engineering would. So almost like the through line even to Clay is there were a lot of engineering best practices that we were trying to bring to operations teams. But yeah, so we worked on this for about four and a half years. We went through YC, we raised from Excel. We sold to a bunch of really cool companies like Ramp, AngelList, Valon, DoorDash. So some really cool and interesting customers to work with. And yeah, in late '24, the business was growing pretty well. We ended up meeting Kareem and Varun through I think a mutual connection. But at the time we had been approached by some other players in the space—some other data engineering companies—who'd always been interested in acquiring the business. So we were kind of in that mindset of we could raise the Series A. We were pretty excited about the business growth but weren't necessarily—we didn't know if this was going to be the billion-dollar outcome that we were trying to get to when we set out to start the business. And so then it was like, well, we should probably join up with a bigger company that already has more traction. And it ended up just really connecting with Kareem and Varun.
turns.zh: 所以我们一直在琢磨各种想法，我的联合创始人在 Uber 工作过，我毕业后在亚马逊工作过，我们都想一起创业。我们都有这样的想法：嘿，我们在非常不同的领域处理不同类型的运营问题，但这些市场运营团队实际上需要像工程团队那样的可观测性解决方案。所以甚至到 Clay 的一条主线是，我们试图将许多工程最佳实践带给运营团队。但是的，我们在这上面工作了大约四年半。我们通过了 YC，从 Excel 融资。我们卖给了许多很酷的公司，比如 Ramp、AngelList、Valon、DoorDash。所以有一些非常酷和有趣的客户可以合作。是的，在 24 年底，业务增长得相当好。我们通过一个共同的联系人认识了 Kareem 和 Varun。但当时这个领域的其他一些参与者——其他一些数据工程公司——曾与我们接触，他们一直有兴趣收购这项业务。所以我们处于这样的心态：我们可以筹集 A 轮融资。我们对业务增长相当兴奋，但不一定——我们不知道这是否会成为我们创业时想要达到的十亿美元成果。然后就是，好吧，我们可能应该加入一家已经有更多牵引力的大公司。最终与 Kareem 和 Varun 真的产生了很好的共鸣。

turns.en: So they already had a lot of traction at that point.
turns.zh: 所以他们在那个时候已经有很多牵引力了。

turns.en: Yeah. I mean, you know—
turns.zh: 是的。我是说，你知道——

turns.en: How big was the company by the way? Sorry.
turns.zh: 顺便问一下，公司有多大？抱歉。

turns.en: It was—I think we joined right as they were 50 people.
turns.zh: 当时——我想我们加入时他们正好有 50 人。

turns.en: And you were how many?
turns.zh: 那你们有多少人？

turns.en: We were five.
turns.zh: 我们有五个人。

turns.en: Okay. So you were like 10% of the company.
turns.zh: 好的。所以你们大约占公司的 10%。

turns.en: Yeah. I think we underappreciated how much of a bet they were taking on us. To bring in 10% of the company in just one day is kind of a—
turns.zh: 是的。我觉得我们低估了他们对我们下了多大的赌注。在一天内引入公司 10% 的人，这有点——

turns.en: Yeah, it's a pretty big bet.
turns.zh: 是的，这是一个相当大的赌注。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: I think it's nice to bring in a scaled team and also perhaps you guys were more on the automation side. What do you think you spiked more versus the original Clay team?
turns.zh: 我觉得引入一个规模化的团队很好，而且也许你们更偏向自动化方面。你认为你们相比最初的 Clay 团队在哪些方面更突出？

turns.en: Yeah. I mean, I think one, we were really deep in building just very robust systems. The story I like to tell is Clay was really focused on PLG and they had really nailed the PLG motion.
turns.zh: 是的。我是说，我认为一方面，我们非常深入地构建非常稳健的系统。我喜欢讲的故事是，Clay 非常专注于 PLG，他们真的把 PLG 模式做得很好。

turns.en: So like we joined the company when it was maybe like 15 to 20 million in revenue, but the biggest contract was really small. Like it was just like so many companies who had found Clay and had just signed up and ended up getting value out of the platform. But they hadn't really moved into mid-market or enterprise sales yet. And I think that was something that we really knew how to do at Avenue. Avenue was hey build systems that could go into DoorDash and Angel kind of more scaled outcome companies.
turns.zh: 我们加入公司时，营收大概在 1500 万到 2000 万美元之间，但最大的合同其实很小。就是有很多公司发现了 Clay，注册了，然后从平台上获得了价值。但他们还没有真正进入中端市场或企业销售。我认为这是我们在 Avenue 真正擅长的事情。Avenue 是那种能进入 DoorDash 和 Angel 这类更规模化成果公司的系统。

turns.en: Would you say that was the biggest learning that you took from Avenue and then applied it to Clay?
turns.zh: 你觉得这是你从 Avenue 学到并应用到 Clay 的最大收获吗？

turns.en: One of the things that I think Clay has done really well is focus really deeply on one customer persona like the go-to-market engineer. And I feel like everything we do is for the go-to-market engineer. And I think at Avenue we had some commercial traction but we never really figured out who our core customer was. We were kind of across a couple of different personas like different company types. And so I think one of the things that is really impressive about Clay is the amount of focus on the single customer persona.
turns.zh: 我认为 Clay 做得非常好的一点是，它非常深入地聚焦于一个客户画像，比如 GTM 工程师。我觉得我们所做的一切都是为了 GTM 工程师。而在 Avenue，我们有一些商业吸引力，但从未真正弄清楚我们的核心客户是谁。我们有点分散在几个不同的画像和不同的公司类型上。所以我认为 Clay 令人印象深刻的一点是对单一客户画像的专注程度。

turns.en: Okay. So you guys join like what was like what was your 90-day plan like like can you maybe like paint a picture of the business at that point and you like okay well what's the plan for the next six months?
turns.zh: 好的。那你们加入时，你们的 90 天计划是什么？你能不能描绘一下当时业务的情况，然后说‘好的，接下来六个月的计划是什么’？

turns.en: So yeah, so we joined Clay and I think the main thing that we were trying to do at Clay when we joined was Clay had a really good business on sort of static lists, right? So I don't know, you throw a dinner, you want to figure out if any of the people who came to the dinner are good customers for you and you could do that in Clay and like that was a good business for them at the time. But if you're trying to build revenue systems, which I guess now it's our new tagline, but if you wanted to build these sort of online systems of someone changes jobs and like you know, they had bought Clay at their previous company, but then maybe they would buy Clay at their next company or like, you know, you kind of wanted to build these online systems for revenue. We didn't really have a great system in place to do that. And so we helped build out their original signals product, which was effectively that. So monitor for new hires, monitor for things like promotions, like any of these events that we could see in the market that you might want to act on and build plays off of. So yeah, so we spent actually the first couple of months doing that and there was a lot of tech overlap with what we had built at Avenue. Like we had very different domains, very different product spaces, but it just ended up being a pretty similar problem. Because it was kind of market observability, wasn't operational observability. It was just like, hey, look at all of these events that we can see in the market and be able to build plays off of that.
turns.zh: 是的，我们加入了 Clay，我认为我们加入时在 Clay 试图做的主要事情是，Clay 在静态列表方面有一个很好的业务，对吧？比如你办个晚宴，你想知道来晚宴的人里有没有你的好客户，你可以在 Clay 里做到，这对他们当时来说是个好业务。但如果你想要构建收入系统——我想这现在是我们的新口号——但如果你想要构建这种在线系统，比如某人换工作了，他们在前公司买过 Clay，但也许他们会在下一家公司买 Clay，或者你想要构建这些在线收入系统。我们当时并没有一个很好的系统来做这个。所以我们帮助构建了他们最初的 signals 产品，实际上就是这个。监控新员工、监控晋升之类的事件，任何我们能在市场上看到、你可能想要采取行动并构建 play 的事件。所以是的，我们实际上花了头几个月做这个，而且与我们在 Avenue 构建的东西有很多技术重叠。虽然我们领域非常不同，产品空间非常不同，但最终问题非常相似。因为它是市场可观测性，而不是运营可观测性。就是，嘿，看看市场上所有这些事件，并能够基于此构建 play。

turns.en: What was the hardest part about building the signals product?
turns.zh: 构建 signals 产品最难的部分是什么？

turns.en: There's a lot of things that were difficult about it and I think one of the things that we didn't appreciate kind of building this was just the diversity of customers that would use it, right? Like I think we've been used to really building things alongside a core set of design partners, but Clay has a lot of different customers and they just have a lot of different needs and different and to the point about go-to-market engineers like they're really creative and so people were building just kind of crazy stuff on top of this.
turns.zh: 有很多困难的地方，我认为我们在构建这个时没有意识到的一点是使用它的客户的多样性，对吧？我觉得我们习惯了与一组核心设计伙伴一起构建东西，但 Clay 有很多不同的客户，他们有很多不同的需求，而且说到 GTM 工程师，他们真的很有创造力，所以人们在这上面构建了一些疯狂的东西。

turns.en: Like what are some examples if you can share? Surprising use cases maybe?
turns.zh: 比如你能分享一些例子吗？也许是一些令人惊讶的用例？

turns.en: I think it was just like some of the scale was just crazy and like I don't remember the exact numbers but you know some people were like really trying to track every customer that they'd ever talked to like where they were like their career progressions like different things that they were posting. So like news articles like it was just like a very scaled out thing.
turns.zh: 我觉得就是有些规模简直疯狂，我不记得具体数字，但有些人真的试图追踪他们交谈过的每一个客户，比如他们的职业发展，他们发布的不同内容。比如新闻文章，就是一个非常大规模的东西。

turns.en: Okay. Yeah. Social mentions, product reviews, gong calls.
turns.zh: 好的。是的。社交提及、产品评论、Gong 通话。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: Okay. Website visitors. There's just a lot. I mean, I think it's one of those things where it's easy to get really lost if you It's easy to just like on day one of play just go like, "Oh my god, I can like react to all these things." And then you just stop reacting cuz you just drown under all these things.
turns.zh: 好的。网站访客。有很多。我的意思是，我觉得这是那种很容易迷失的事情，如果你在 play 的第一天就容易说‘天哪，我可以对所有这些事情做出反应。’然后你就不再反应了，因为你被所有这些事情淹没了。

turns.en: Yeah. I mean, that that's the kind of the beauty and the scary part about Clay is just like there's a ton you can do and like it's a really powerful platform, but yeah, it can be a little overwhelming.
turns.zh: 是的。我的意思是，这就是 Clay 的美妙和可怕之处，你可以做很多事情，它是一个非常强大的平台，但确实可能有点让人不知所措。

turns.en: So did you join as like an engineering manager and now you're head of AI like like when did that transition happen?
turns.zh: 所以你是作为工程经理加入的，现在你是 AI 负责人，这个转变是什么时候发生的？

turns.en: Yeah. Yeah. So actually I joined to build out the signals product which is almost not really AI right it's just sort of you know
turns.zh: 是的。是的。实际上我加入是为了构建 signals 产品，那几乎不是真正的 AI，对吧，它只是那种你知道的

turns.en: pipelines
turns.zh: 管道

turns.en: pipelines yeah it's just sort of a regular system that you might build at kind of any company I would say a lot of people used to use Zapier for this kind of stuff right
turns.zh: 管道，是的，它只是那种你可能在任何公司都会构建的常规系统，我会说很多人以前用 Zapier 做这类事情，对吧

turns.en: yeah and but like Zapier kind of let's just call it politely didn't evolve with the times
turns.zh: 是的，但 Zapier 那种，我们客气地说，没有与时俱进

turns.en: there's all sorts of advantages of kind of building the system with all of the other stuff that you can do with clay right like I don't know if I think of a zap year as just A to B data movement, right? Like if you have all of this data piped into the same place, you can kind of do all these interesting things where it's like, hey, I only want to react when there's like three people from this company that move to the same company or something like that, right? Like um you kind of have the statefulness as well. It's kind of nice.
turns.zh: 用 Clay 可以做的所有其他事情来构建系统有各种优势，对吧？我不知道，我把 Zapier 看作只是从 A 到 B 的数据移动，对吧？如果你把所有数据管道到同一个地方，你可以做所有这些有趣的事情，比如‘嘿，我只想当这家公司有三个人搬到同一家公司时才反应’之类的，对吧？就像你也有状态性。这挺好的。

turns.en: Yeah. Back to the transition to like head of AI. So like so you built the signals product. What now?
turns.zh: 是的。回到向 AI 负责人的转变。所以你构建了 signals 产品。然后呢？

turns.en: Well, yeah. So at the time, I mean, you know, we joined when the company was 50 people, engineering team was about 20 folks. Um, I mean Clay at the time, yeah, I mean to this day there was a huge part of the business was using agents to qualify and enrich stuff like search the web, find data points about companies, like actually use those data points to do things. And at the time there was one person working on that and so I think he was maybe 24 so you know like pretty fresh out of school and he actually ended up leaving to go start a company of his own. you know, was super excited for him, but you know, we were this, you know, really AI forward company that had zero people working on AI. So, it was kind of scary.
turns.zh: 嗯，是的。当时，你知道，我们加入时公司有 50 人，工程团队大约 20 人。嗯，我是说 Clay 当时，是的，直到今天，业务的很大一部分是使用智能体来筛选和丰富信息，比如搜索网络、查找公司的数据点，实际使用这些数据点来做事情。当时只有一个人在做这个，我想他大概 24 岁，你知道，刚毕业，他后来离开去创办自己的公司了。你知道，为他感到非常兴奋，但你知道，我们是一家非常 AI 前沿的公司，却零个人在做 AI。所以有点可怕。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: Um, and so like we were basically like, hey, like we really need to rep prioritize like make sure that we're actually investing in this. And there was all this other stuff that we wanted to do in AI at the time.
turns.zh: 嗯，所以我们基本上说，嘿，我们真的需要重新优先考虑，确保我们真正投资于此。而且当时我们还想在 AI 方面做很多其他事情。

turns.en: Like we really just had AI as part of our workflows, but not building workflows or sort of all the things that ended up becoming really important in the last year and a half. So basically I shifted my attention over to one, just kind of trying to get that into a good place and help build out that team, help build out the road map and figure out kind of what we wanted to do with AI and agents and kind of build out the strategy.
turns.zh: 我们当时只是把 AI 作为工作流的一部分，但并不是在构建工作流，也不是在做过去一年半里变得非常重要的那些事情。所以基本上我把注意力转移到了一件事上，就是试着把这块做好，帮助组建团队，制定路线图，弄清楚我们在 AI 和智能体方面想做什么，并制定战略。

turns.en: You said at that point in time AI was part of workflows. It wasn't really a big part of it. What were those things? And then what was on your road map that you were like, 'Oh, we're going to totally overhaul this.'
turns.zh: 你说当时 AI 是工作流的一部分，但并不是很重要。那些东西是什么？然后你的路线图上有什么是你觉得‘哦，我们要彻底改造这个’的？

turns.en: You know, we had an agent product in Clay actually really early. So I think like November of 2023, so like a year after ChatGPT, we had an agent product that would search the web, actually structure data, do structured data extraction from that, and you could use that in your Clay workflow. So you could imagine building a column that's like 'hey who's the CEO of this company' and it would go off and search the web and kind of structure this data into a cell output. And I think this is a huge part of the Clay business to this day, but it's not super inspiring as like 'hey AI is going to change go-to-market.' You know I'm an engineer by background. I used Cursor, Claude Code came out in February of '25 and I was like you know this is a pretty different thing than what engineers had been doing. And so we were like hey this is clearly the direction that engineering is going and you know there's probably something in go-to-market as well that we're going to see as well. Basically trying to bring the same shift that Cursor brought to engineering actually to go-to-market in that domain. That was the majority of our road map I would say was actually just building agents into the product, letting people build and configure go-to-market plays with agents.
turns.zh: 你知道，我们其实很早在 Clay 就有了一个智能体产品。所以我想是在 2023 年 11 月，也就是 ChatGPT 之后一年，我们有一个智能体产品，可以搜索网络，实际结构化数据，从中进行结构化数据提取，你可以在 Clay 工作流中使用它。所以你可以想象构建一列，比如‘嘿，这家公司的 CEO 是谁’，它会去搜索网络，并将这些数据结构化到单元格输出中。我认为这至今仍是 Clay 业务的重要部分，但它并不那么令人兴奋，不像‘嘿，AI 将改变市场推广’。你知道我有工程师背景。我用了 Cursor，Claude Code 在 25 年 2 月推出，我当时觉得这和工程师们一直在做的事情相当不同。所以我们觉得嘿，这显然是工程的发展方向，而且市场推广领域可能也会出现类似的东西。基本上就是试图把 Cursor 带给工程的那种转变，实际带到市场推广领域。我会说我们路线图的大部分实际上就是把智能体构建到产品中，让人们用智能体构建和配置市场推广策略。

turns.en: What's the first thing after signals that you start with that was like a real hit?
turns.zh: 在信号之后，你开始做的第一件真正大受欢迎的事情是什么？

turns.en: Yeah so we launched, so like that was the direction that we were trying to go into was just agents building more of your go-to-market plays and you know improving them over time but that came a bit later but we launched Sculptor.
turns.zh: 是的，所以我们推出了，那个方向就是我们试图进入的，就是智能体构建更多的市场推广策略，并随着时间的推移改进它们，但那是后来才出现的，但我们推出了 Sculptor。

turns.en: Oh, Sculptor first. Okay. I had Claygent pulled up.
turns.zh: 哦，先推出 Sculptor。好的。我原本以为先推出的是 Claygent。

turns.en: Yes. Yes. So, Claygent. Claygent is what we had in workflows. Yeah. So, it's just like Claygent were basically you would have an agent that would crawl the web, structure data and put it in a table and it's again like it's a huge part of the Clay platform. I think actually most people think of Clay as... and yeah, we did a ton more work on Claygent. So, I don't know. I mean we basically rebuilt the entire Claygent stack. We did a ton of work to just make this scale to the level that it is today. I mean again like the business has basically 10xed since we joined and like...
turns.zh: 是的。是的。所以，Claygent。Claygent 是我们在工作流中已有的。是的。所以，就像 Claygent 基本上就是你会有一个智能体，它会爬取网络，结构化数据并放入表中，这同样是 Clay 平台的重要部分。我想实际上大多数人认为 Clay 是……是的，我们在 Claygent 上做了大量工作。所以，我不知道。我的意思是我们基本上重建了整个 Claygent 技术栈。我们做了大量工作，只是为了让它扩展到今天的水平。我的意思同样是，自从我们加入以来，业务基本上增长了 10 倍，而且……

turns.en: You can imagine that more people are actually using Clay agents even than the business growth and so there was just a ton of work to get that into a good place.
turns.zh: 你可以想象，实际上使用 Clay 智能体的人甚至比业务增长还多，所以有大量的工作要把它做好。

turns.en: I was going to say, you know you made the statement about the business 10x since you joined. You could draw a nice chart here, was like you know Jeff joins here and look at the shareholder value that we've added. That's right.
turns.zh: 我想说，你知道你提到自你加入以来业务增长了 10 倍。你可以在这里画一个漂亮的图表，就像你知道 Jeff 在这里加入，看看我们增加的股东价值。没错。

turns.en: Uh where is it? Yeah, that's right. Yeah, I have a new acquisition.
turns.zh: 呃，在哪里？是的，没错。是的，我有一项新的收购。

turns.en: I mean, you know, so we're here, right?
turns.zh: 我的意思是，你知道，所以我们在这里，对吧？

turns.en: Yeah. Was I late 24, so just very...
turns.zh: 是的。我是 24 年底，所以非常……

turns.en: Yeah. Okay. Uh yeah. So I mean Okay. So and again just for people who again many of whom they are engineers or they are new to the overall GTME ecosystem. Clay agents are just basically the same Clay interface but everything is exposed to the agent. Agent can do everything that a human could do.
turns.zh: 是的。好的。呃是的。所以我的意思是好的。所以再次，为了那些再次，其中许多人是工程师，或者他们对整个 GTME 生态系统不熟悉。Clay 智能体基本上就是相同的 Clay 界面，但一切都暴露给智能体。智能体可以做人类能做的任何事情。

turns.en: Yeah. I would almost think of Clay agents as like what sales reps would have been doing like a few years ago, right? Which is like, hey, like for all of my leads, I'm going to go figure out like, I don't know, like are they a plumbing company or a news company, right? Like they'll do some categorization. They might research like, oh, do they have the number of employees that I would expect to be able to sell to this company. You can imagine they have access to all of the things you can do in Clay. They're just natively in your table and they have access to the web as well.
turns.zh: 是的。我几乎会把 Clay 智能体想象成几年前销售代表会做的事情，对吧？就像，嘿，对于我所有的潜在客户，我要去弄清楚，比如，我不知道，他们是管道公司还是新闻公司，对吧？就像他们会做一些分类。他们可能会研究，哦，他们是否有我期望的能够向这家公司销售的人员数量。你可以想象他们可以访问你在 Clay 中能做的所有事情。他们只是原生地在你的表格中，并且他们也可以访问网络。

turns.en: Doesn't that data come from like ZoomInfo like all these other data providers? I would almost think of Claygent as one an agentic way to get some of this data. But primarily it's the public web. Okay. So yeah.
turns.zh: 那些数据不是来自像 ZoomInfo 这样的所有其他数据提供商吗？我几乎会把 Claygent 想象成一种智能体方式来获取一些数据。但主要是公共网络。好的。所以是的。

turns.en: And then so Sculptor.
turns.zh: 然后所以 Sculptor。

turns.en: Yes. So Sculptor we launched I think almost just about a year ago. And the idea with Sculptor was like hey we can go like one level of abstraction up which is like you know Claygents are sort of the things doing each of the tasks in your workflow right like they're qualifying they're scoring enriching like I don't know doing copywriting. Sculptor is the thing that's actually building those workflows to you know coordinate these Claygents together.
turns.zh: 是的。所以 Sculptor 我们推出了，我想几乎大约一年前。Sculptor 的想法是，嘿，我们可以上升一个抽象层次，就像你知道 Claygent 是执行工作流中每个任务的东西，对吧，比如它们在进行资格认定、评分、丰富数据，比如我不知道，做文案写作。Sculptor 是实际构建这些工作流以协调这些 Claygent 的东西。

turns.en: Okay.
turns.zh: 好的。

turns.en: You can think of it almost like orchestrator.
turns.zh: 你几乎可以把它想象成编排器。

turns.en: Yeah. Yeah. Like Sculptor is like building the table structure and then like Claygents are filling in the table cells.
turns.zh: 是的。是的。就像 Sculptor 是构建表格结构，然后 Claygent 填充表格单元格。

turns.en: Can you talk about like what the stack is you used to build it?
turns.zh: 你能谈谈你用来构建它的技术栈是什么吗？

turns.en: I think we, I'll describe it. I think we've just learned so much since then. I can describe sort of what we've...
turns.zh: 我想我们，我会描述一下。我想从那以后我们学到了很多。我可以描述一下我们……

turns.en: Maybe like talk about the evolution. I think that would be really interesting.
turns.zh: 也许谈谈演变过程。我觉得那会很有趣。

turns.en: Yeah. Yeah. So we launched Sculptor in September of last year. So we basically were building it through the summer of last year and I think at the time, you know, it was like Sonnet 3.5 or maybe it was around then I think, you know, so the models were way less advanced. I think like people just knew less about how to build agents properly. This is like really figuring things out. Sculptor ended up being, you know, we had a bunch of different tool interfaces to access, read, update the Clay platform and we basically gave it to a model in a loop and we spent a lot of time on sort of system prompt optimization and tool definition optimization and I think it came out well, but it was way less expressive than I think even Claude Code was at the time and definitely like the agents that people are building now. I think we just had way less ability to sort of do these, I don't know, long horizon things too.
turns.zh: 是的。是的。所以我们在去年九月推出了 Sculptor。所以我们基本上在去年夏天构建它，我想当时，你知道，是 Sonnet 3.5 或者大概那时候，你知道，所以模型远没有那么先进。我想人们只是对如何正确构建智能体了解得更少。这真的是在摸索。Sculptor 最终是，你知道，我们有一堆不同的工具接口来访问、读取、更新 Clay 平台，我们基本上把它交给一个循环中的模型，我们花了很多时间在系统提示优化和工具定义优化上，我想结果不错，但它比当时甚至 Claude Code 的表达能力差得多，绝对也比不上人们现在构建的智能体。我想我们只是能力差得多，无法做这些，我不知道，长视野的事情。

turns.en: The way I describe it is like Sculptor was really good at doing things like, 'Hey, add this column that does this.' It was not good at doing things like 'build me an outbound campaign that's going to deliver 10 qualified meetings on my calendar.'

turns.zh: 对对，他们就是这样要反馈的吧？他们就说给我反馈 ID。但我确实觉得，你们作为智能体构建者，基本上需要自己的版本，以便回传给实验室。然后更强大的版本是，你把所有 bug 报告打包，称之为基准测试。

turns.en: And then just be like look you guys are bad on this.
turns.zh: 然后就说，看，你们在这方面很差。

turns.en: Yeah, what do you think about that?
turns.zh: 嗯，你觉得怎么样？

turns.en: I think it's good. It takes a bit more work, but you could probably have like a grad student work on it with you. And just go like, 'Hey, like these are my past like 500 bug reports.' Categorize them up, group them up, clean them up, remove PII, and that's a benchmark. And that's a paper for you.
turns.zh: 我觉得不错。这需要多花点功夫，但你可以找个研究生和你一起做。然后说，‘嘿，这是我过去 500 份 bug 报告。’把它们分类、分组、清理、去除个人身份信息，那就是一个基准测试。那对你来说就是一篇论文。

turns.en: Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. This is like an area where I mean, we're thinking about this. I think it's a great area to partner with companies like I feel like there companies do this all day.
turns.zh: 嗯。嗯。嗯。这是一个我们正在考虑领域。我觉得这是一个与公司合作的绝佳领域，感觉有些公司整天都在做这个。

turns.en: Like Sierra was super early to this because obviously Cartek was GPT-3 and like they were like okay like each of our main verticals we do tobench airline retail telecom and like please optimize for this and like it's basically the please make my business better for me thanks.
turns.zh: 就像 Sierra 很早就这样做了，因为显然 Cartek 是 GPT-3，他们就说好吧，我们的每个主要垂直领域，我们做航空、零售、电信的基准测试，请为此优化，基本上就是‘请让我的业务更好，谢谢’。

turns.en: Yeah, I mean we do spend some time thinking about like what does performance in go to market or performance in sales look like, kind of what would a sales optimized model look like. But yeah, I mean we're early on. We haven't looked into doing a public benchmark, but I think it could make sense.
turns.zh: 是的，我是说我们确实花时间思考，比如在进入市场或销售方面的表现是什么样的，一个销售优化的模型会是什么样。但是的，我们还在早期。我们还没有研究做公开基准测试，但我觉得这可能有意义。

turns.en: Yeah. No, I think the grad students will love to work with you and look, New York has tons of them like yeah, you'll find somebody. I just think like this is one of those things where like as a marketing guy and you know, I'm primarily a marketing guy and maybe a bit of community, maybe a bit of content and all that. This achieves your goals and it achieves the lab's goals. This is like a very much a win-win win in terms of community understanding of your problems too. So this is one of those things that if I can encourage you to publish those kind of things, you know, it's it can be high leverage.
turns.zh: 嗯。不，我觉得研究生会喜欢和你合作，看，纽约有很多这样的人，是的，你会找到人的。我只是觉得，作为营销人员，你知道，我主要是营销人员，也许还有点社区、内容之类的。这实现了你的目标，也实现了实验室的目标。这在社区理解你的问题方面也是双赢的。所以这是那些事情之一，如果我能鼓励你发表这类东西，你知道，它可以有高杠杆效应。

turns.en: You'll get all the engineers in New York to like come out of their den, you can do that.
turns.zh: 你会让纽约所有的工程师都走出他们的窝，你可以做到。

turns.en: Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. I mean, it's just another way of forcing them to look at data and do evals and label them, which they don't want to do. So you have to come up with creative ways to make them enjoy their work that they actually normally wouldn't do.
turns.zh: 嗯。嗯。嗯。我是说，这只是另一种迫使他们查看数据、做评估和标注的方式，而他们不想做这些。所以你必须想出创造性的方法，让他们享受他们通常不会做的工作。

turns.en: Yeah. Yeah. I do think we have a good flywheel of this internally where we have real good market engineers who spend a lot of time thinking about like how would we find pockets of customers that we should reach out to or how would I build scoring for my customers or whatever, all these things. So we have some in-house talent there, but we probably haven't connected that flywheel as much as we should.
turns.zh: 嗯。嗯。我确实认为我们内部有一个很好的飞轮，我们有非常优秀的市场工程师，他们花很多时间思考，比如我们如何找到应该接触的客户群体，或者我如何为我的客户构建评分等等。所以我们有一些内部人才，但我们可能没有把这个飞轮连接得足够好。

turns.en: Actually you talked about coding agents a lot. Do you have any things you want coding agents to get a lot better at over the next six months, 12 months, and that would help the Clay CLI?
turns.zh: 实际上你谈了很多编码智能体。你有没有希望编码智能体在未来 6 个月、12 个月内大幅改进的地方，那会帮助 Clay CLI？

turns.en: Yes. And maybe this connects the question, but model capability is being able to look at an agent trace and figure out what's wrong with it. Maybe it's just too self-reflective, but it still really doesn't work. So we're trying to build the loose forms of continual improvement, but it's not even continual improvement, but like, hey, here's a trace. It was really long. The agent probably got confused. Can you tell me where it got confused? And I think agents are still not good at this. They just have the wrong intuition about what's wrong. They're like, 'Oh, well, this took a long time.' And it's like, 'No, no, that makes sense.' It's just completely wrong, I think, most of the time. And so if you try to connect it the whole way where it's like hey just download the bad traces, have agents look at those and then improve those over time, that just doesn't work. Similarly, agents writing their own prompts maybe works in some sense, but if you're just like hey fix the agent performance based on this thing, that doesn't really work. So I don't know, we're still handwriting a lot of skills. We're doing a lot of stuff there, and that feels like a tractable solvable problem too.
turns.zh: 是的。也许这连接了问题，但模型能力是能够查看智能体轨迹并找出问题所在。也许这太自我反思了，但它仍然真的不起作用。所以我们试图构建持续改进的松散形式，但甚至不是持续改进，而是像，嘿，这里有一个轨迹。它真的很长。智能体可能搞糊涂了。你能告诉我它在哪里搞糊涂了吗？我认为智能体仍然不擅长这个。它们对错误的直觉不对。它们会说，‘哦，这花了很长时间。’然后就像，‘不，不，那是合理的。’我认为大多数时候它们完全错了。所以如果你试图把它连接起来，就像嘿，只需下载坏的轨迹，让智能体查看那些，然后随着时间的推移改进那些，那就不起作用。同样，智能体编写自己的提示词也许在某种意义上有用，但如果你只是说嘿，根据这个东西修复智能体性能，那并不真的有效。所以我不知道，我们仍然手写很多技能。我们在那里做了很多工作，那感觉也是一个可处理、可解决的问题。

turns.en: You guys have Sculpt I think coming up. Yes. Is there anything that you are going to be launching that you could potentially tease?
turns.zh: 我想你们即将推出 Sculpt。是的。有什么你们将要发布的东西可以透露一下吗？

turns.en: Clearly Sculptor.
turns.zh: 显然是 Sculptor。

turns.en: In 10 days.
turns.zh: 在 10 天后。

turns.en: Yes. So I do think we will launch a whole host of new features for our bet on the good market engineer and so giving them new tools in their toolbox.
turns.zh: 是的。所以我确实认为我们将推出一大堆新功能，押注于优秀的市场工程师，给他们工具箱中的新工具。

turns.en: All right. Do you have anything? I think no, I think it's really you've been really open about your journey. I think like people who haven't tried Clay, you know honestly I conceptually understood Clay, I didn't understand the depth, I didn't understand the work that you've done. I have use cases now for my two businesses and you know what is like when you explain Clay to an engineer friend what do you usually tell them to try?
turns.zh: 好的。你有什么要说的吗？我想没有，我觉得你对自己的旅程真的很开放。我觉得像那些没试过 Clay 的人，老实说，我概念上理解 Clay，但我不理解深度，我不理解你所做的工作。我现在有两个业务的使用案例，你知道，当你向工程师朋友解释 Clay 时，你通常告诉他们尝试什么？

turns.en: I don't know. I think it's like kind of the stuff that you're trying to do in go to market. I would just try asking Clay like try asking the agent to build that.
turns.zh: 我不知道。我觉得就像你在进入市场时试图做的事情。我会试着问 Clay，就像试着让智能体构建那个。

turns.en: Yeah. And see what happens.
turns.zh: 嗯。然后看看会发生什么。

turns.en: See what happens.
turns.zh: 看看会发生什么。

turns.en: All right. Well, thank you so much for spending some time with us and good luck for your big conference.
turns.zh: 好的。非常感谢你抽出时间，祝你的大会顺利。

turns.en: Thank you so much. Thank you. Thanks.
turns.zh: 非常感谢。谢谢。谢谢。

tldr.en: Clay builds GTM agents that qualify, enrich, and research across the whole table like sales reps.
tldr.zh: Clay 构建的 GTM 智能体像销售代表一样，在整个表格中完成资格审核、数据丰富和研究。

tldr.en: Model routing is key: frontier models for orchestration, cheaper ones for simple tasks; auto mode beats manual selection.
tldr.zh: 模型路由是关键：前沿模型用于编排，更便宜的模型用于简单任务；自动模式胜过手动选择。

tldr.en: Institutional courage is the most important thing; keep pushing and don't over-engineer agents or jump into post-training early.
tldr.zh: 机构勇气是最重要的；持续推动，不要过度设计智能体或过早进入后训练。
